(London, May 5, 2026) Isembard, the manufacturing company for critical industries, today announces a strategic partnership with Dexory to manufacture components for its autonomous warehouse robots and support production scaling across the United Kingdom and the United States.

Demand for autonomous robotics is accelerating across logistics, defense, and industrial sectors at an incredible pace, placing increasing pressure on manufacturing capacity. Isembard's model, combining advanced machine tools, robotics, and software across owned and franchise factories, is designed to meet this demand with speed, precision, and resilience.

Together, the companies will scale production to a run rate of thousands of units per year by the end of 2027, supporting global demand for Dexory's platform while strengthening sovereign manufacturing capability across both regions.

Alexander Fitzgerald, Founder and CEO of Isembard, said: "Dexory is building one of the most important robotics platforms from Europe. By combining their product with our manufacturing system, we can move faster from design to scaled production than traditional supply chains allow. This is exactly the kind of partnership we are building Isembard for."

Founded in London in 2024, Isembard is rebuilding the industrial base the West needs. We do this through building, software-first factories that produce components for the critical industries that will define the next century – defense, aerospace, energy, and more.

We are uniquely operating a manufacturing franchise model – it enables new and existing factory owners to join a high-performance manufacturing company supported by MasonOS, Isembard's proprietary operating system for quoting, scheduling, production, and quality control.

To deliver this, Dexory designs, builds, and deploys its hardware and software end-to-end, ensuring full control over data quality, system performance, and reliability. The platform integrates seamlessly into existing operations, improving inventory accuracy, reducing errors, and unlocking significant operational efficiency at scale.

Dexory's technology is deployed by leading global logistics providers including GXO, DHL, and NFI, as well as manufacturers such as Stellantis, Samsung, and GE Appliances, across sectors including retail, pharmaceuticals, and eCommerce.
Isembard opens London's largest factory since WWII - ADS Advance

Component manufacturing is a market worth $1.8 trillion a year, yet small businesses account for 95% of production and are rapidly disappearing: the average owner is over 65 and 40% plan to retire within five years.

Isembard’s model, combining owned and franchisee factories with its proprietary agentic operating system, MasonOS, is built to close that gap, giving operators the technology, brand, engineering standards and customer demand to run high-performance manufacturing businesses from day one.

The Southwark site spans 160,000 sq ft and will serve as Isembard’s global head office alongside a working precision factory, producing components for aerospace, defence and robotics customers, including

The purpose behind the location and scale of the manufacturing operation is to tap into London’s vast technology talent pool combined with daily proximity to the operational reality of running a large-scale production site.

Isembard expects headcount at the Southwark HQ to grow from 35 today to 200 by the end of 2027, spanning production, software, manufacturing and robotics automation engineering alongside wider support functions for the group’s factory network.

The opening caps Isembard’s fastest year of growth to date. The company has gone from four factories at the start of 2026 to 15 today, opening its first sites in continental Europe, in France and Germany and onboarding 10 new franchise operators.
Isembard is targeting 100 owned and franchisee factories across the UK alone by the end of 2028, a programme expected to create 2,200 high-skilled jobs.

Alexander Fitzgerald (above), Founder and CEO of Isembard, said: “Manufacturing is the origin of our security, prosperity and sense of purpose as nations. No one has opened a factory like this in London since the Second World War and that tells you how far our industrial base has been allowed to shrink.

“Bringing production back onshore is the work of the next decade. What we need now are the brightest engineering minds of our generation to join us. Engineers, you have nothing to lose but your chains.”
